decided: If an earlier pull-request step of the same command failed, such as opening the pull request at propose or the final push at archive, the closing commit does nothing at all. The user is left with the recovery commands that failure printed, and they still work.
alternatives: let the closing commit run anyway, and remove from the recovery commands propose prints the commit of the propose record
why: The existing rule for a failed pull-request step says no later pull-request step runs; it names only the steps that open the pull request and finish it at archive, and it lets orbit's own records still be written. This change puts the closing commit under that rule as a pull-request step, because running it would commit the propose record orbit writes, retry a push that just failed, and make the printed recovery fail.

relies_on.title: PR actions are workflow-body choreography (zero engine git)

defines.definition: the commit and push at the end of a command, which orbit makes only when the project turns committing or pushing on
